soil.notes: No reliable source names the native soil. Race coverage notes softer dirt is brought in before the national and that roost is largely rocks. A track-guide site calls it decomposed granite, but that site's other data was wrong, so it is not used.

layout.notes: Foothills track above Denver at roughly 6,100-6,400 ft. Uphill start into a right-hander. Thin air cuts engine power so jumps are harder to clear and riders cannot use power to cover mistakes.

conditions.dry: Rocky roost is a constant hazard; riders steer off the main line to avoid it.
conditions.wet: After a rainy week (2025) the dirt stayed soft and rutty all day with ruts everywhere; unrepaired sections got Endurocross-like.
conditions.late_day: Deteriorates within each moto; crews rework sections between motos.
conditions.watering_prep: Imported dirt worked in before nationals; heavy equipment between motos.
conditions.seasonal: Public riding Wed-Fri 10am-dusk, weekends 9am-5pm per directory. Hosts an early-June Pro national; hosted the 2010 Motocross of Nations.

rider_reports.says: Analyst: after rain all week the track was soft and rutty everywhere; altitude sapped power and fitness. Advice: carry power deeper and brake closer to the corner since the soft dirt slows the bike; teams remapped for the uphill start.
Analyst: brutal ruts and rocky roost; weight the outside peg on exits, lift the inside leg in ruts, and jump right-to-left onto a tabletop as the ground falls away.
